question: Can the five ASEANO studies identified by CvSU be crosswalked to public reports, and does that report set provide Imus River fish-species evidence?

projectContext.parentProject: Biophysical Characterization, Vulnerability, and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed as part of ASEANO
projectContext.primaryCrosswalkFinding: CvSU's January 2021 newsletter lists all five study titles and assigns Studies 1-3 to DLSU-D and Studies 4-5 to CvSU. It explicitly assigns Study 4 and Study 5 titles; it does not assign a PEMSEA report URL or file identifier to each title.
projectContext.dateDiscrepancy: The CvSU newsletter gives January-June 2021; the CvSU Research Center listing gives November 2020-April 2021. The difference remains unresolved.

studyCrosswalk.newsletterTitle: Knowledge, Attitude, and Practices of Selected Communities on Plastic Pollution and Economic Valuation of Imus River, Cavite, Philippines
studyCrosswalk.publicOutputTitle: ASEANO Project Report: Assessing Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices Concerning Plastic Waste Along Imus River
studyCrosswalk.evidence: The CvSU newsletter lists the Study 1 title under DLSU-D. PEMSEA's report title and description match the KAP and economic-valuation scope and identify the DLSU-D output as Subproject 1. The two numbering systems are not assumed to be identical: PEMSEA's DLSU-D Subproject 1 is crosswalked to overall Study 1 by the matching title and the CvSU list.

studyCrosswalk.newsletterTitle: Survey on Plastic Litter along Imus River, Cavite, Philippines
studyCrosswalk.publicOutputTitle: ASEANO Project Report: Survey on Plastic Litter Along Imus River
studyCrosswalk.evidence: The CvSU newsletter's Study 2 title and the official PEMSEA report title both identify a DLSU-D Imus River plastic-litter survey. The public report is labeled DLSU-D Subproject 2; its subproject number is not treated as the overall ASEANO study number without the newsletter title crosswalk.

studyCrosswalk.newsletterTitle: Assessment of the Socio-Economic Implications of Plastic Pollution along the Imus River: Basis for Policy Framework
studyCrosswalk.publicOutputTitle: ASEANO Project Report: Social Implications of Plastic Pollution Mitigation Initiatives Along the Imus River
studyCrosswalk.evidence: The CvSU newsletter's Study 3 title and the official PEMSEA page's socioeconomic/social-implications description align. PEMSEA labels the accessible PDF DLSU-D Subproject 3. The retrieved PDF cover/title marks it as a rough draft, so it is not represented as a final version.

studyCrosswalk.newsletterTitle: Mapping and Characterization of Imus River Watershed Using GIS and RS
studyCrosswalk.publicOutputTitle: ASEANO Project Report: Mapping and Characterization of the Imus River Watershed
studyCrosswalk.evidence: The CvSU newsletter explicitly assigns the matching Imus watershed GIS/remote-sensing study as Study 4. The official PEMSEA report carries the matching mapping title and CvSU authorship; a prior focused review confirmed it as this component output.

studyCrosswalk.newsletterTitle: Mapping of Sources and Concentration of Plastic Waste Generation in the Imus River Watershed
studyCrosswalk.publicOutputTitle: ASEANO Project Report: Mapping of Sources and Concentration of Plastic Waste in the Imus River Watershed
studyCrosswalk.evidence: The CvSU newsletter explicitly assigns the near-identical plastic-source mapping title as Study 5 under CvSU. The official PEMSEA publication page labels the report CvSU Subproject 2, describes mapping plastic sources and waste-generation hotspots, and the report cover identifies CvSU authors. This confirms the report as the Study 5 component; it is not the complete parent-project deliverable.

additionalPublicOutputs.title: ASEANO Project Report: Assessment of Water Quality along Imus River
additionalPublicOutputs.status: listed in the official ASEANO forum program as a DLSU-D output; not one of the five titles in the CvSU January 2021 list; already covered as a separate pollution/water-quality evidence lane where sources are available
additionalPublicOutputs.fishEvidence: Water-quality assessment is not a fish inventory or current safety determination.

additionalPublicOutputs.title: Study on Plastic Use and Waste Management in the Food Service Industry
additionalPublicOutputs.status: listed as a separate industry-sector output in the official ASEANO forum program; not assigned to the five CvSU newsletter studies
additionalPublicOutputs.fishEvidence: Food-service plastics research is not a fish inventory.

additionalPublicOutputs.title: ASEANO LGU toolkit and project proceedings
additionalPublicOutputs.status: official project knowledge/communication products outside the five-study title list
additionalPublicOutputs.fishEvidence: Toolkit and proceedings are not a substitute for specimen or occurrence records. The forum's separate Bacoor fish-tissue remark remains unidentified and unresolved.

fishEvidenceScreen.question: Do these five study outputs establish fish taxa, a species checklist, specimen-level occurrence, or an Imus fish survey?
fishEvidenceScreen.result: No fish taxa, taxonomic checklist, specimen table, fish-sampling protocol, voucher, or site-resolved occurrence was verified in the five crosswalked public outputs.
boundedReportFindings: Study 1's full searchable report describes household/community KAP and economic valuation. Its method includes a valuation variable for vegetables and fish harvested from the river, but the reviewed passages provide no fish taxon, specimen record, sampling station, or taxon-specific catch data.
Study 2 surveys plastic litter, water microplastics, and physicochemical water conditions; it is not a fish survey.

Study 3's PEMSEA publication page describes socioeconomic research. The accessible 108-page PDF is marked ROUGH DRAFT; bounded text searches found fish-related community-consumption discussion but no species terminology or evidence of fish sampling. It is not treated as a final fish study.
Study 4 maps and characterizes the watershed; its map legend's fish-pond land-use class is not biological evidence.

The report discusses fish and aquatic impacts in its general background and cited literature; these are not Imus River observations. Its stated objectives and methods concern plastic-waste sources, amounts, coordinates, and hotspot analysis, not local fish sampling.
fishEvidenceScreen.separateLead: The 2022 ASEANO forum proceedings mention CvSU fish-tissue microplastics research in Bacoor, but no report, taxon, collection site, date, method, dataset, or voucher is provided. It is not assigned to Imus River or to any of these five report outputs.
fishEvidenceScreen.interpretation: This is a bounded review of the public ASEANO reports and available searchable text, not evidence that no fish research exists elsewhere in CvSU or the wider watershed project.

rightsReview.decision: Retain report titles, bibliographic metadata and short source findings only. Do not republish maps, tables, measurements, report text, underlying GIS, or datasets without item-specific rights review.

limitations: The CvSU newsletter is a planned-study description, not a final project report or proof that every expected output was completed exactly as planned.

The PEMSEA report labels use institutional subproject numbering that differs from the overall Study 1-5 numbering in the CvSU newsletter; links are made from matching titles, scope, and named institution.
The accessible Social Implications PDF is labeled ROUGH DRAFT and should not be treated as a validated final report.
No item-specific reuse license for the report text, maps, data, or GIS layers was verified.
No findings here establish current water quality, food safety, fishing legality/access, or fish absence.

Official Study 2 report metadata and previously reviewed full report.

Official Study 4 report metadata and previously reviewed full report.
Official Study 5 report metadata, CvSU Subproject 2 label, scope, authorship context, and downloadable full report.
Official forum output schedule showing the ASEANO component outputs and identifying the separate Bacoor fish-tissue research lead.

nextAction: Continue the separate public-source search for the unidentified Bacoor fish-tissue study and for any final CvSU biophysical characterization outputs. Require taxa, exact site/waterbody, dates, methods, identification or voucher support, and reuse terms before making fish occurrence claims.
